summary.headline: Kanpur Plastipack Q4 FY26 standalone PAT rose ~14% YoY to INR14.53 crore, but a INR3.65 crore DFIA income reversal cut other operating income to negative INR2.9 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone total income was INR183.1 crore (up ~6.16% YoY), with EBITDA of INR25.06 crore (13.69% margin) and PAT of INR14.53 crore. FY26 total income rose 26.26% to INR726.67 crore, EBITDA reached INR74.75 crore (10.29% margin) and PAT was INR38.19 crore (up ~68%). Management attributed the Q4 hit to government suspension of import duty on polypropylene until 30 June, which removed the value of DFIA licences. Management guided to 10% top-line growth in FY27 with margins similar to current levels, and flagged a softer order book in the near term from customer inventory correction.

financial_highlights.value: INR3.65 crore; other operating income negative INR2.9 crore
INR112 crore (short-term borrowing INR78 crore, GECL loans INR23.8 crore, long-term loans INR9.01 crore)

segments.name: FIBC (Unit 2, existing)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 18,000 tpa; FY26 dispatches 14,351 tonnes and production about 15,000 tonnes, i.e. ~83% utilisation (management cited 85% earlier). Management says margins depend on stitching minutes rather than tonnage.

segments.name: Non-woven technical textiles (new, needle-punch)
segments.commentary: Commercial production targeted from September 2026 (machine 1) and December 2026 (machine 2). FY27 revenue guided at INR20-25 crore; FY28 at INR100-120 crore (one reference said INR100-125 crore) with 15-16% EBITDA margin. FY28 volume about 8,000-9,000 tonnes.

segments.name: Premium PP yarn via ESSEKAN JV with Essegomma
segments.commentary: JV marketing company expects INR20-25 crore of sales in FY27; Kanpur Plastipack manufactures and sells to ESSEKAN at about a 20% markdown (about INR20 crore). Management guided 15% EBITDA for both the marketing JV and manufacturing; capex about INR3 crore.

segments.name: Trading and other income
segments.commentary: Other income comprises forex gains and trading interest income; management could not say how it will trend in FY27. Manufacturing-only EBITDA margin was 12.17%, per the presentation cited in Q&A.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth of about 10% (10-15% range mentioned for steady growth), with margins similar to current levels.
Non-woven: FY27 revenue INR20-25 crore with no loss expected; FY28 revenue INR100-120 crore at 15-16% EBITDA at steady state.

FIBC Unit 3 (6,000 tpa target): building complete by May 2026; about 1,800 tonnes produced in FY27 and run-rate of 2,400 tpa by end FY27; full 6,000 tpa over about 4-5 years, worth about INR130 crore revenue, with about INR40 crore incremental revenue from converting fabric capacity to FIBC.

Raw material 'new normal' expected at USD1,200-1,350 per tonne versus USD1,000 earlier; DFIA income expected to resume once import duty suspension (till 30 June) ends, at about INR3-3.5 crore per quarter on average.
Gross margin goal of 45-47% in manufacturing, given rising FIBC share.
capex_capacity: FIBC Unit 3: building to be complete by May 2026; ~100 tonnes produced in March 2026 (run-rate 1,200 tpa); 2,400 tpa run-rate targeted by end FY27.
Non-woven: two needle-punch machines (first by September, second by December 2026); capacity about 10,000 tonnes; fibre (not captive yarn) is the raw material.
Warehouse expansion and automation initiatives expected to complete by September 2026.
Capital advances rose to INR13.75 crore from INR1.46 crore, for non-woven machinery, FIBC building and other machinery.
Acquired Valex Ventures (UK), a B2C-linked business that has not yet delivered immediate success.
demand_pricing: Order lead times fell from 6-8 weeks to 3-4 weeks; customers are placing smaller, more frequent orders amid inventory correction and high prices. Management expects order book to be a challenge in Q1 and Q2 FY27.
Polypropylene prices rose from about USD1,000/t to about USD1,700/t (~65%); Indian PP averaged INR1,500 vs China about INR1,250 in March 2026, which hampers Japan entry.
Europe 56.5%, South America 21.8%, North America 16.9% of exports; North America fell from 21% to 16% of exports due to US tariff disruption.
End-use mix: food and agriculture 52%, industrial packaging 23%, construction 12%, automotive 7%, mining and building materials 6%.
Pass-through of raw material costs to customers is per kg, not percentage-based, which management says supports margin conversion when prices rise.

qa_highlights.question: When will the new unit start commercial production and what revenue will it contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Unit 3 produced 100 tonnes in March 2026 at a 1,200 tpa run-rate; about 1,800 tonnes expected in FY27, exiting at 2,400 tpa. Full 6,000 tpa is worth about INR130 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 11% Q4 margin sustainable and what is FY27 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will sustain and gave 10-15% growth, later narrowed to about 10% top-line growth.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company have a price pass-through clause for Europe?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, pass-through is per kg rather than percentage, so a rise in raw material cost lifts the percentage of RM in selling price (e.g. 50% rising to about 60% in the example).

qa_highlights.question: What is the DFIA reversal and its run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: The reversal covered income up to 31 December 2025, because the duty suspension wiped out licence value. DFIA averages about INR3-3.5 crore per quarter once it resumes.

qa_highlights.question: How much did ESSEKAN and non-woven contribute, and what are the margins?
qa_highlights.answer: ESSEKAN sales INR20-25 crore with Kanpur at a 20% markdown; both marketing JV and manufacturing expected at about 15% EBITDA. Non-woven FY28 target INR100-120 crore at 15-16% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Asia's contribution low, and is Japan on the back burner?
qa_highlights.answer: Asia is price-competitive with local makers and shorter lead times; Japan is still a focus, with Tokyo Pack exhibition in Sept-Oct 2026, though China and Vietnam currently have cheaper PP.

qa_highlights.question: What is FIBC utilisation given sales of 14,352 tonnes?
qa_highlights.answer: Production was about 15,000 tonnes against 18,000 tpa installed, about 83% utilisation; management said real capacity is stitching-time based.

risks_watch: Raw material volatility: PP prices at ~USD1,700/t in the latest spike; management expects a new normal of USD1,200-1,350/t, with the government duty suspension (till 30 June) and DFIA income reversal affecting other income.
Order book softness in Q1-Q2 FY27 as customers buy smaller and more often; lead times down to 3-4 weeks.
Non-woven ramp-up: first revenue only from September 2026; 35% effective time availability in FY27 and 70% utilisation assumed; no OEM approvals yet, only trial and sampling orders.
Europe concentration at 56.5% of exports; North America share fell to 16%.
Labour skill and stitching-capacity constraints for the expanded FIBC capacity; Valex Ventures (UK) B2C business yet to show success; Japan entry delayed by Chinese PP pricing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term strategy and margins, but cautious on near-term demand and order book, and vague on exact figures (other income, DFIA quarterly amounts, growth guidance). Management was candid about the DFIA reversal and frankly acknowledged baby-step progress in non-woven.
key_quotes: We have continued to strengthen our presence in core industrial packaging, while gradually building capabilities in value-added segments such as premium polypropylene yarns and non-woven fabrics.
Order book will remain a challenge in this quarter and the next quarter, but we do not see that there is a structural change in the consumption pattern.
We do not expect that we have to reduce our capacity.
So, the new normal could be anywhere between USD1,200 and USD 1,350 for us as our raw material.

adds.what: FIBC Unit 3 (6,000 tpa target; 2,400 tpa run-rate by end FY27)
Non-woven needle-punch machine 1 (~10,000 t capacity across two machines)

growth.why: Management guides ~10% FY27 top-line growth with margins held near current levels, backed by FIBC Unit 3 (1,800 t output in FY27, 2,400 tpa run-rate by end-FY27) and non-woven revenue of INR20-25 crore, though it flagged a softer order book in Q1-Q2 FY27 from customer inventory correction.
